David / team —

Quick findings from initial triage:
- Error mode: elevated 503/504 from inference nodes in us-west-2 starting ~11:14 PST.
- Telemetry: KV cache pressure + connection queuing on a subset of instances. Not a full AZ outage but a concentrated node pool saturation (likely due to a large batch job from a new tenant).
- Impact: median p95 token latency up ~18x for affected shards; traffic is unevenly distributed.

Mitigation options (pros/cons):
1) Immediate geo-swap (route Greenline to us-east-1 and drain us-west-2): fastest customer-visible remediation. Risk: cold KV caches in target region, slight token-cost increase, potential ordering delay for in-flight sessions.
2) Scoped node drain + throttling in us-west-2: preserves session locality but slower to stabilize (10–20m).
3) Model fallback to smaller instance class in region: reduces latency but may reduce throughput/quality.

Recommendation: approve option 1 (geo-swap to us-east-1) now while we do a rolling node replacement and postmortem. I have the geo-failover playbook ready (attached) and can run the swap once we have authorization. Estimated customer visible recovery: 3–8 minutes after route switch; whole stabilization 20–30 minutes.

Attachments: support_log_bundle.zip, geo-failover-playbook.pdf

— Rishi
SRE Lead, Inference Runtime
